title: Scout (Adaptive Parallelism audit): matrix of adaptive-parallelism-program.md P0-P4 and P12 against source and tests, plus scheduler telemetry row shapes
spec: Objective: test-surface and telemetry audit of the merged scheduling work. Read .orchestrator/adaptive-parallelism-program.md sections P0, P1, P2, P3, P4, P12 and .orchestrator/roadmap-completion-program.md sections P7 and P9. For EVERY requirement bullet in AP P0, P1, P2, P3, P4, P12 decide from the SOURCE: implemented_tested | implemented_undertested | partial | missing | experimental_gated, with file:line and covering test names (tests/test_interference.py, test_critical_path.py, test_schedlog.py, test_daemon.py, test_scorecard.py, test_baseline.py). Inspect orchestrator/interference.py (classify rules: which deterministic signals exist: exact file, scope overlap, same dir, shared tests, shared config, migration, generated artifacts, interface/consumer; graph_signal; graph_fresh_for), critical_path.py, schedlog.py, daemon.py dispatch (lines 594-860: wave_row and dispatch row keys), daemon.py stale_check/_record_stale_check/_stale_rebase (1050-1123), gate() 1124-1211, merge_reviewed 1257-1352, merge.py, scorecard.py --parallelism section (grep parallelism, concurrency, queue_wait, merge_wait, critical_path, dependency_wait, idle), baseline.py _parallelism_deltas, cli.py flags. Specific questions: (1) P0 telemetry: which of max/avg concurrent executors and Claude workers, executor idle, worker idle, queue wait, execution time, review time, merge wait, wall clock, critical path, dependency wait, quota blocking, merge conflicts, rebase failures, stale failures, fix rounds from concurrent changes, duplicated scout/review work are computed, from which pipeline stamps (dispatched_at, claimed_at, first_green_at, gated_at, merged_at ...), and which stamps are never written (e.g. merged_at on Planner merge() calls, review start/finish). (2) Skip reasons recorded in dispatch.jsonl: list the exact reason vocabulary in code. (3) P1 hard/soft rule coverage vs brief list; is there a scope-size or module signal; any caching for large ready sets. (4) P2 graph signal: what edges are used, freshness check, fallback. (5) P3 waves: is capacity analysis part of select_wave or only slots; do waves respect executor role/complexity/budget/cooldown per task or only global slots. (6) P4 ranking: which brief inputs (downstream depth, blocked descendants, est duration, review duration, fix-round probability, unlock) are used. (7) P12 stale: which of the six signals (scoped files, public interface, relevant tests, graph relationships, dependency changed, overlapping earlier merge) are checked; what a stale row records; rebase path behaviour. (8) Exact JSON keys written to runs/sched/dispatch.jsonl, waves.jsonl and any stale log, and the runs/<date>.jsonl usage row keys (role, task, tokens, usd, executor, duration, ts). Output format, STRICT, under 5500 characters: one line per requirement 'AP.P<n>.<short-key> | <status> | <file:line,...> | <tests or none> | <gap <=12 words>'; then 'ROWS: dispatch={keys} waves={keys} stale={keys} runs={keys}'; then 'STAMPS_MISSING: ...'; then 'UNCERTAIN: ...'. No prose.
acceptance: Every AP P0-P4 and P12 requirement bullet appears as one matrix line with status, evidence, tests, gap
ROWS and STAMPS_MISSING lines list the exact telemetry keys and the pipeline stamps never written
Result under 5500 characters, structured lines only, derived from source
